analysis.investment_thesis: DIACABS scores near-zero on both Magic Formula legs: Earnings Yield is ~0.8% (EBIT ₹67 Cr / EV ~₹8,340 Cr) vs. the 12% minimum, and ROIC is roughly 3–4% (₹67 Cr EBIT on ₹2,048 Cr assets) vs. the 20% threshold. A company with negative book equity priced at 74.9× earnings is pure speculation, not value.
key_strengths: Revenue turnaround is real — grew from ₹0 in 2022 to ₹1,115 Cr in 2025, suggesting the restructured business is operating again
Debt dramatically reduced from ₹2,355 Cr (2024) to ₹463 Cr (2025), implying successful resolution/restructuring
Operating in a capex-heavy power infra sector with strong Indian government tailwinds (grid expansion, renewables)
key_risks: Negative equity of -₹714 Cr means liabilities still exceed assets — technically insolvent on book value basis
Earnings yield of ~0.8% is catastrophically below Magic Formula threshold; market is pricing in years of future growth that hasn't materialized
Accumulated losses from 2015–2023 (-₹805 Cr in FY17 alone) destroyed the balance sheet; reserves stand at -₹767 Cr
red_flags: Negative book value (-₹714 Cr equity) — P/B of -10.95 is not a value metric, it's a warning sign
Debt drop from ₹2,355 Cr to ₹463 Cr in one year likely reflects a haircut/write-off, not repayment — creditors absorbed losses
₹34 Cr net profit in FY25 justifying ₹7,884 Cr market cap (P/E 74.9×) is speculative excess
EBITDA margin 6% in FY25 (₹67 Cr on ₹1,115 Cr) — margins have not recovered to pre-distress levels (2012–2014 were 10–12%)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on DIACABS produces two near-zero scores. Earnings Yield: EBIT of ₹67 Cr divided by an Enterprise Value of ~₹8,340 Cr (₹7,884 Cr market cap + ₹463 Cr debt − ₹7 Cr cash) yields 0.8% — I need 12%+ for a stock to even enter my screen. Return on Capital: ₹67 Cr EBIT on ₹2,048 Cr total assets (negative equity makes traditional NWC + NFA calculation unreliable, but any reasonable cut gives ROIC of 3–5%) — I need 20%+. Both legs fail badly, and the Magic Formula explicitly requires BOTH to be high.

The story here is a company that imploded spectacularly (₹805 Cr net loss in FY17, negative equity since FY22, near-zero revenue until FY23) and has partially restructured. The debt collapse from ₹2,355 Cr to ₹463 Cr in a single year screams haircut, not operational cash generation — creditors took losses so equity holders could survive. A ₹7,884 Cr market cap on ₹34 Cr of net profit in the first profitable year post-restructuring is the market paying for a dream. My formula doesn't buy dreams; it buys high-ROIC businesses at cheap earnings yields. DIACABS offers neither.
